key_insight: Frozen medical LLM embeddings can act as a shared space to combine structured EHR variables and discharge notes for primary ICD category prediction.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help automate diagnosis coding and support portable EHR representations across hospitals and datasets.
method: Built a MIMIC-IV cohort of 13,645 admissions from the 10 most frequent primary ICD-10 codes, grouped into 7 categories.
Serialized structured EHR variables into narrative text and combined them with leakage-pruned discharge notes.
Extracted hidden states from 5 layers of a frozen MedFound-Llama3-8B model and trained linear probes; compared with XGBoost and PLM-ICD baselines, plus a small adapter for MIMIC-III transfer.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-IV, the combined probe achieved 87.69% strict accuracy and 91.45% medical accuracy, outperforming single-modality probes and baselines; a 2M-parameter adapter enabled transfer to MIMIC-III with 5% target labels.
watch_item: Results depend on careful leakage pruning and dataset-specific label structure, so real-world deployment may require site-specific validation and retraining.
paper_title: Primary ICD Category Prediction using LLM-based Probing
